subject: Saving intermediate variable in model block

messages.author: f8a4136bfeaed71c
messages.subject: Saving intermediate variable in model block
parts:
Hi all,

I have a problem of saving an intermediate variable in model block. For short view, below is a segment of codes:

for(i in 1:N){
mu1[i] = betaadl[1]*age[i] + betaadl[2]*gender[i]+ betaadl[3]*IDInter3[i] + betaadl[4]*IDInter5[i]
+ betaadl[5]*IDInter6[i] + betaadl[6]*IDInter7[i] + betaadl[7]*IDInter9[i] + betaadl[8]*IDInter10[i]
+ betaadl[9]*IDInter12[i]
   + (betaadl[10] + betaadl[11]*age[i] + betaadl[12]*gender[i]+ betaadl[13]*IDInter3[i] + betaadl[14]*IDInter5[i]
+ betaadl[15]*IDInter6[i] + betaadl[16]*IDInter7[i] + betaadl[17]*IDInter9[i] + betaadl[18]*IDInter10[i]
+ betaadl[19]*IDInter12[i])*year[i]
   + betaadl[20]*ex6201[i] + betaadl[21]*alone[i]
   + betaadl[22]*ik4a01[i] + betaadl[23]*ik4b01[i] + betaadl[24]*ik4c01[i] + betaadl[25]*ik4d01[i] + b0[ID[i]];
}

I want to save "mu1". I know that we can specify "mu1" in transformed parameters block. However, I cannot do it because "mu1" depends on ex6201, ik4a01, ..., ik4d01, which are binary (integer) variables, and cannot define in any parameters blocks. If I specify "mu1" in parameters block, then its components must be in parameters, but cannot because of integers.

Do you have any suggestion to overcome this?

Thank you,
Tran.

P/S: Full codes can be found in the attachment.

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Saving intermediate variable in model block
parts:
Hi Tran,

You can put it in the generated quantities block. You'll have to redo the calculation, but the repeated calculation is very fast relative to anything in the transformed data and model blocks. 


Daniel
